Error: Error in S[1, 1] : incorrect number of dimensions

I have seen this issue on the lavaan messsage boards but I have not found an adequate solution. I am attempting to use n=20 imputed data sets (using mice) to run a simple cross-sectional mediation analysis

#imputing data
imp.unordered <- mice(scc_mi.v1, maxit = 10, method = "pmm", m = 20, seed = 1121)

#making dataframe usable to lavaan
mice.imp.unordered <- list()
for(i in 1:20) mice.imp.unordered[[i]] <- complete(imp.unordered, action=i, inc=FALSE)

#model specification
scc.med <- '     
 #direct effect
             odi_new~c*bpi_0avg_g

# b-path
              odi_new~b*scc_0ttl_g

#  a-path
              scc_0ttl_g~a*bpi_0avg_g

indirect effect (a*bs)
              ab1 := a*b #define new parameter

total effect
              total := c + (a*b) #define new parameter using ":="
 '
#running lavaan with imputed datasets
 sem.unordered <- lavaan.mi(scc.med,
               data=mice.imp.unordered,
               meanstructure=T,estimator="mlr")

Error in S[1, 1] : incorrect number of dimensions

Any help would be appreciated.

David Reed, PhD
COIN VA Puget Sound
Associate Health Fellow

I think you didn't save a stack of imputed data sets as a single data set, which is the only way it could be saved in a single spreadsheet (or text file to be imported as such).  You have a list of imputed data sets, so you can just save that object using

saveRDS(impList, file = "impList.rds")

Imported with

impList <- readRDS(file = "impList.rds")

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Error: Error in S[1, 1] : incorrect number of dimensions
parts:
I tried running one imputation with normal lavaan, and it did not converge.  I expect your problem was only that you ran the bare-bones lavaan() function without specifying any residual variances, which I had not noticed before (sorry).  That is taken care of automatically when you use the sem() wrapper.  Here's a script I ran without error:

impList <- readRDS("impList.rds")

#model specification
scc.med <- '    
 #direct effect
             odi_new ~ c*bpi_0avg_g
# b-path
              odi_new ~ b*scc_0ttl_g
#  a-path
              scc_0ttl_g ~ a*bpi_0avg_g
# indirect effect (a*bs)
ab1 := a*b #define new parameter
# total effect

total := c + (a*b) #define new parameter using ":="
'

# running lavaan with ONE imputed dataset
fit1 <- sem(scc.med, data = impList[[1]], estimator = "mlr")
summary(fit1)

# running lavaan with ALL imputed datasets
sem.unordered <- sem.mi(scc.med, data = impList, estimator = "mlr")
summary(sem.unordered)

Terrence D. Jorgensen
